findings.description: The eviction loop compares len(self._keys_by_country), the number of distinct countries, with max_entries. The number of cached rates is len(self._entries). The cache therefore never evicts until there are more than max_entries countries, so it grows without bound by postal code. The old lru_cache(maxsize=4096) capped the number of rates, so this removes that bound.
findings.title: Capacity check counts countries instead of entries

findings.description: Entries expire by TTL but are never removed from _entries or _keys_by_country when they are replaced. The expired key is re-stored, which is harmless for the set. However, `_evict_oldest` and `invalidate_country` assume the indexes stay in sync. `invalidate_country` does `del self._entries[key]`, which raises KeyError if a key was already evicted. This is currently guarded because eviction removes the key from the set, but the capacity-check bug above leaves the eviction path wrongly gated.
findings.suggestion: Use `self._entries.pop(key, None)` in invalidate_country to be robust.
findings.title: clear() does not reset stats while invalidate_country also ignores bookkeeping consistency

findings.description: put_country_rates replaces the table and only then invalidates the cache. A concurrent lookup in the gap can still be served the old cached rate. A lookup that misses can load a rate and store it either side of the replace, so it may cache a rate from the old table after the invalidation if it started before. The class docstring claims the lock rules this out, but replace_country is not performed under the cache lock.
findings.suggestion: Perform the replace and the invalidation atomically, for example by running the table swap while holding the cache lock.
findings.title: Table replaced before cache invalidation; stale rate can be cached in between

findings.description: Normalising keys can map different input prefixes (e.g. 'ab 1' and 'AB1') to the same key. The later entry silently overwrites the earlier one, which may have a different rate, and no error is reported.
findings.suggestion: Detect duplicate normalised keys and return a 400.
findings.title: Distinct prefixes can collapse after normalisation and silently overwrite each other
